name: Microsoft West Texas Data Center (Project Kilby)

profile.reading:
Project Kilby is a co-located natural gas power plant in West Texas that will supply a Microsoft-operated data center under a 20-year power purchase agreement announced on 22 June 2026. The plant is being developed by Energy Forge One, a wholly owned Chevron subsidiary, with Engine No. 1. Chevron says it will deliver about 2.67 GW, built in phases, mostly from GE Vernova turbines with additional units from Solar Turbines.

Chevron expects first power in 2028 and a final investment decision by the end of 2026, subject to conditions. The plant is designed to supply Microsoft directly rather than through the regional grid, and plans to use brackish groundwater instead of fresh water.

The 2.67 GW is generating capacity, not data center IT load. Chevron's announcement says only West Texas; trade press reports Reeves County near Pecos, which is not confirmed by the operator.

sources.title: Chevron Signs 20-Year Power Agreement with Microsoft for West Texas Data Center
Chevron to fuel massive Microsoft data center in Texas using natural gas

profile.capacity_note: 2.67 GW is the power plant's stated generating capacity, not the data center's IT capacity, which has not been published.
